Cropland
In 1975, approximately 700 acres on Tract II and 1575 acres on Tract III were utilized for dry cropland. This amounts to about 7.4 percent of the lease area. Disturbed grasslands, which represent areas once used for agriculture but which have reverted naturally or as a result of grass seeding to rangeland, account for about 985 acres on Tract II and 680 acres on Tract III. Presumably, reversion of these lands to grazing resulted from a lack of suitability for farming, although increased demand for agricultural products could result in increased tillage in the future. Most of the agriculture activity within the boundaries of the leases is concentrated in gently rolling upland areas, and it may be assumed that essentially all such land will eventually be mined.
The 1975 value of dry cropland in the area has been estimated at $200 to $350 per acre (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 b). Income forgone when dryland agricultural land is mined is estimated to be $30.33 per acre per year (Big Horn County Situation Statement Emphasizing Agriculture, 1972; U.S. Department of Agriculture, Committees for Rural Development, 1972), although this figure is highly dependent on market fluctuations and other factors.
